questions.q: How many help requests have employees raised, and how many were solved on time?
questions.briefing: Employees raised **10,352** help requests between Jan 2025 and Sep 2026. **86.3%** of the solved ones were answered within the promised time, and only **30** are still open today.
insights: **8,904** requests were closed inside their promised time; **1,418** took longer.
High-priority requests must be solved in 1 day, medium in 2 days and low in 4 days.
Employees who rated the service gave an average of **4.0 / 5**.

questions.q: How many help requests do we get each month?
questions.briefing: We get about **479** help requests a month. The busiest month was **September 2026** with **771** requests.
insights: Volume went from **314** in Jan '25 to **767** in Aug '26 as the company grew.
The latest month is partial data (up to 30 Sep), so ignore the small dip at the end.

questions.q: What do employees ask HR for help with the most?
questions.briefing: **Payroll** questions are the most common, making up **24.8%** of all requests, followed by **Leave** and **Reimbursement**.
insights: Salary-related topics (Payroll + Tax) account for **32.3%** of requests.
Tax is the least asked topic with **778** requests.

questions.q: How quickly did employees start using the AI Copilot after it launched?
questions.briefing: The AI Copilot went live in **March 2026** and already handles **71%** of all requests in Sep 2026 — **2,248** conversations in total.
insights: Adoption grew every month after launch, mostly at the cost of Email and Portal requests.
Employees now prefer a quick chat over waiting for an email reply.

questions.q: How many questions does the AI Copilot answer without needing an HR person?
questions.briefing: Since launch, the AI Copilot has fully solved **1,644** of **4,486** requests (**36.6%**) without needing an HR person, saving the HR team a lot of effort.
insights: The AI answers instantly, while the HR team needs about **1.8 days** on average.
Policy, leave and payslip questions are the easiest for the Copilot to handle.

questions.q: Which way of asking for help (Copilot, email, portal...) gets answered fastest?
questions.briefing: **AI Copilot** is the fastest way to get help — solved in **0.47 days** on average, versus **1.8 days** for the slowest channel.
insights: Average rating by channel: AI Copilot **4.1**, Teams Chat **3.99**, Portal **4.0**, Email **3.93**.

questions.q: Which type of request is most often solved on time, and which is most often late?
questions.briefing: **Benefits** requests are solved on time most often (**87.8%**), while **Reimbursement** needs attention at **85.5%**.
insights: The gap between best and weakest topic is **2.3 points**.

questions.q: How long does an employee wait for the first reply?
questions.briefing: Half of all requests get a first reply within **40 minutes**. The average wait is **53.3 minutes**; AI Copilot replies are **instant**, while HR-team replies take about **63.4 minutes**.
insights: **68%** of requests get a first reply within an hour.

questions.q: How happy are employees with the help they get?
questions.briefing: Employees rate our help **4.0 out of 5** on average, and **75%** gave 4 or 5 stars (5,681 ratings).
insights: 5-star is the most common rating with **2,198** votes.
Only **3.8%** of employees gave a 1-star rating.

questions.q: Which departments ask for help the most?
questions.briefing: **Engineering** raises the most help requests (**38.2%**), mainly because it is the biggest team. Hover over a block to see the exact count.
insights: Top 3 teams — Engineering, Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics — raise **58%** of requests.

questions.q: How urgent are the requests, and how many are still open?
questions.briefing: **16%** of requests are high priority. Only **30** of all 10,352 requests are still open — almost everything gets closed.
insights: Open requests: **2** high, **12** medium, **16** low priority.

questions.q: On which days and in which topics are we busiest?
questions.briefing: **Monday** is the busiest day with **2,128** requests. The hottest spot is **Payroll** on **Mon**.
insights: Darker blocks mean more requests — useful for planning when HR staff should be available.

questions.q: How many leave days does each type of leave give per year?
questions.briefing: A full-time employee gets **12 Casual**, **12 Sick** and **18 Earned** leave days every year. Interns get 6 Casual and 6 Sick days. Special leaves like Maternity and Marriage come on top.
insights: Casual and Sick leave expire on 31 December; up to 15 unused Earned Leave days carry forward.
Leave taken without balance is treated as Loss of Pay.

questions.q: How many leave requests were approved, rejected or are still waiting?
questions.briefing: Out of **26,714** leave requests, **97.0%** were approved. **315** were rejected and **106** are still waiting for a decision.
insights: Only **1.2%** of requests get rejected — managers rarely say no.

questions.q: In which months do people take the most leave?
questions.briefing: In 2025 people took the most leave in **Oct** (**2,452 days**). Monthly leave in 2026 is higher than in 2025 because the company is bigger. Oct–Dec 2026 only show leave approved so far.
insights: Leave days per month in Jan–Sep 2026 are about **152%** of the same months in 2025.
October 2025 was the busiest month (festival season), with **2,452** leave days.

questions.q: Which type of leave do people use the most?
questions.briefing: **Earned Leave** is the most used leave type (**38%** of all days), followed by **Casual Leave** and **Sick Leave**.
insights: Special leaves (marriage, maternity, paternity, bereavement) together use **8425** days.

questions.q: Which departments take the most leave?
questions.briefing: In 2025, **Customer Success** took the most regular leave (Casual, Sick, Earned) per person (**26.3 days a year**) and **Information Security** the least (**18.4 days**). Numbers are per employee-year, so team size and joining dates do not skew the picture.
insights: Spread between the highest and lowest team is **7.9 days** per person.

questions.q: How many days does a manager take to approve leave?
questions.briefing: Managers decide on a leave request in **1.2 days** on average. **83%** of requests are decided within 2 days.
insights: The most common wait is **Same day**.

questions.q: How much leave do employees have left on average?
questions.briefing: An employee still has about **4.9 Casual**, **6.9 Sick** and **7.3 Earned** leave days left for 2026, after using **4.6**, **2.6** and **7.0** so far.
insights: Casual and Sick leave expire at year-end, so remaining days should be used before 31 December.

questions.q: Which departments have used up most of their leave?
questions.briefing: So far in 2026, the company has used **42.1%** of all leave. **UI/UX Design** leads at **45.0%**, while **AI / ML** has used only **38.2%**.
insights: Teams with low usage may need a nudge to take a break before leave lapses.

questions.q: How many employees are almost out of leave?
questions.briefing: **97** employees (7% of 1,442) have fewer than 6 leave days left across all leave types, while **120** still have more than 30.
insights: Employees with very low balances are at risk of taking Loss-of-Pay leave.

questions.q: Which months are the busiest for each type of leave?
questions.briefing: The heaviest leave month in 2025 was **Oct** (**2,445 days**). The single busiest combination is **Earned Leave** in **Sep** with **798 days**.
insights: Plan project deadlines around the darker months to avoid staffing gaps.

questions.q: How early do people apply for their leave?
questions.briefing: Employees apply **6.2 days** ahead on average. **44%** of requests come with 3 days notice or less, usually sick or emergency leave.
insights: Longer leaves (Earned, Marriage, Maternity) are planned weeks in advance.

questions.q: What are the company holidays this year?
questions.briefing: The company has **11** public holidays in 2026. **4** are still to come — the next one is **Gandhi Jayanti** on **02 Oct**.
insights: Holidays that fall on weekends are not counted as leave days.

questions.q: How much does the company pay in salary each month, before and after deductions?
questions.briefing: In Sep 2026 the company paid **₹20.17 Cr** in gross salary and **₹17.30 Cr** took home after deductions — **14%** went to PF, tax and other deductions. Monthly salary cost has grown **65%** since Apr 2025.
insights: Payroll grew from **728** to **1,481** employees paid per month.
Take-home includes any reimbursements paid through the payslip.

questions.q: What does a salary consist of (basic, HRA, allowances, PF)?
questions.briefing: A typical employee costs **₹1.5 L** a month. **Basic salary** is the largest part (**41%**), followed by special allowance and HRA.
insights: Employer PF, gratuity and insurance are paid by the company on top of take-home — they are part of the CTC, not the salary credited to your bank.

questions.q: What gets deducted from salaries (PF, tax, other)?
questions.briefing: Since Apr 2025, **₹37.36 Cr** has been deducted from salaries. **Income tax (TDS)** is the biggest deduction at **89%**, followed by Provident Fund at **8%**.
insights: Employees paid **₹33.39 Cr** in income tax (TDS) in total, against **₹3.03 Cr** into Provident Fund.
PF is calculated at 12% of basic salary up to the ₹15,000 monthly wage ceiling.

questions.q: Which departments are paid the highest on average?
questions.briefing: **Engineering** has the highest average salary package (**₹21.4 L a year**), while **UI/UX Design** has the lowest at **₹12.1 L**.
insights: Averages are for current employees and include leadership roles in each team.
L = Lakh (1 Lakh = ₹1,00,000) per year.

questions.q: How many days of pay are lost each month due to unpaid leave?
questions.briefing: Employees lost **239 days of pay** (Loss of Pay) since Apr 2025 — about **13** days a month, affecting around **7** people each month.
insights: Loss of Pay happens when leave is taken without balance or an employee is absent without approval.

questions.q: How many salaries were paid on time?
questions.briefing: **100.0%** of all salaries (18,563 of 18,563) were credited on or before the planned salary date. Every payslip has been paid.
insights: Salary is credited on the last working day of the month; the payslip is released the same day.

questions.q: How are employees spread across salary ranges?
questions.briefing: Most employees (**399**, 28%) earn in the **₹8–12 L** range. The average package is **₹18.2 L** and the middle value is **₹12.2 L** a year.
insights: **21%** of employees earn under ₹8 L a year, while **393** earn above ₹20 L.
L = Lakh per year (CTC).

questions.q: How much was the average pay raise in each of the last three years?
questions.briefing: The average pay raise in the **April 2026** cycle was **8.8%** for **727** employees, compared with **9.5%** in 2025 and **8.8%** in 2024.
insights: The number of employees receiving a revision grew from **294** to **727** as the company expanded.

questions.q: Do better performers get bigger raises?
questions.briefing: Yes — better performers get bigger raises. Employees rated **5** received **18.0%** on average, while those rated **1** received **0.0%**.
insights: Policy guideline: raises of 0%, 4%, 8%, 12% and 18% for ratings 1 to 5.

questions.q: Why were salaries revised (yearly raise, promotion, correction)?
questions.briefing: **85%** of salary changes were the normal yearly increment. **141** high performers earned an extra merit increment and **88** employees got no raise.
insights: Policy guideline: raises of 0%, 4%, 8%, 12% and 18% for performance ratings 1 to 5.

questions.q: When is the salary credit date each month?
questions.briefing: Salary is credited on the **last working day** of every month. The next salary date is **30 Oct 2026**; attendance and reimbursement claims must be in by **25 Oct**.
insights: Claims submitted after the cut-off are paid in the next month's payroll.

questions.q: How much extra do employees receive in their salary from reimbursements?
questions.briefing: Reimbursements added **₹2.12 Cr** to employees' pay since Apr 2025 — about **1.0%** of all take-home. In Sep 2026, **763** people received **₹15.1 L** extra.
insights: Approved claims are paid together with salary in the payroll month they are approved for.

questions.q: What benefits can employees get, and what does each one cover?
questions.briefing: Employees can choose from **11 benefit plans** across insurance, retirement, allowances, wellness and learning. Most are paid fully by the company.

rows: Self, spouse and up to 2 children; cashless hospitalisation; sum insured by level (Rs 5L / 7.5L / 10L)

insights: Health insurance covers self, spouse and up to 2 children; parents can be added through the Parental Top-up.

questions.q: How many employees have joined each benefit plan?
questions.briefing: **Group Health Insurance** and the other core plans cover all **1,343** active full-time employees. Among optional benefits, **Meal Card** is the most popular.
insights: Health, life, accident and PF are automatic for every full-time employee.
Wellness check-ups, counselling and the learning budget don't need enrolment, so they are not counted here.

questions.q: Do employees cover only themselves, or their family too?
questions.briefing: **45%** of employees cover only themselves under health insurance. **742** have added their spouse, children or parents.
insights: Health insurance (Medisure) is automatic; employees choose the coverage type when they join.

questions.q: How much does the company pay versus the employee for each benefit?
questions.briefing: The company pays **₹41.0 L** a month towards benefits, while employees contribute **₹30.3 L**. That means the company covers **57%** of the total cost.
insights: Group health insurance and Provident Fund are the biggest company costs.
Only plans with a monthly contribution are shown.

questions.q: How much does the company spend on benefits every month?
questions.briefing: The company now spends **₹41.8 L** every month on employee benefits — up from **₹70.2K** in Q1 '20.
insights: Spend grows in line with headcount as every new full-time employee joins health insurance and PF.

questions.q: How many family members are covered, and who are they (spouse, children, parents)?
questions.briefing: **1,585** family members are covered today. **Spouses** (757) and **children** (562) make up most of them; **266** are parents.
insights: Another **783** dependents were removed (for example after an employee left).

questions.q: What age are the family members covered?
questions.briefing: Covered family members are on average **25.1 years** old. **35%** are children under 13, and **5%** are over 60.
insights: Insurers price risk by age, so this helps plan premium costs for parents and seniors.

questions.q: How many people have joined benefit plans over the years?
questions.briefing: Health insurance members grew from **23** to **1,369** since 2020. Among optional plans, **503** use the Meal Card today.
insights: Membership drops when employees leave, so the lines follow headcount.

questions.q: Which departments have the most employees using benefits?
questions.briefing: **44%** of employees use at least one optional benefit (Meal Card, Parental Top-up or NPS). **Marketing** leads with **56.2%**.
insights: Optional benefits need the employee to opt in, so this shows who is making use of them.

questions.q: How many benefit plans are active, new or ended?
questions.briefing: Of **8,870** benefit enrolments, **6,098** are active, **104** are waiting to start and **2,668** have ended (mostly when employees left).
insights: Pending enrolments become active after the waiting period (e.g. 30 days for the parental top-up).

questions.q: How many expense claims were made, approved and paid, and for how much money?
questions.briefing: Employees raised **15,845** expense claims worth **₹2.60 Cr**. **87%** were approved and **₹2.15 Cr** has been approved or paid out.
insights: **1,854** claims were rejected and **181** are still being reviewed.

questions.q: How much do employees claim each month?
questions.briefing: Employees now claim about **₹17.8 L** a month, up from **₹5.3 L** in Apr 2025. Around **83%** of the money claimed is approved.
insights: Claims grow with headcount, because most are monthly benefits like internet and mobile.

questions.q: Which expenses cost the company the most?
questions.briefing: **Internet / Broadband** is the biggest expense (**₹55.0 L**, 26%), followed by **Business Travel** and **Relocation**.
insights: Small recurring claims (internet, mobile, gym) add up to **43%** of all money paid out.

questions.q: Which types of claims are mostly approved, and which are mostly rejected?
questions.briefing: **Learning & Certification** claims are approved most often (**89.5%**). **Business Travel** claims have the most rejections (**19.0%** rejected).
insights: Higher-value claims (travel, relocation) go through manager + finance approval and are checked more strictly.

questions.q: Why do claims get rejected?
questions.briefing: Out of **1,854** rejected claims, **41%** were rejected for "**submitted after the allowed window**" and **38%** for "**receipt missing**". Both are easy to avoid.
insights: Submit within the allowed window and always attach the receipt for claims above the receipt limit.

questions.q: How many days does it take to approve a claim?
questions.briefing: A claim is decided in **4.4 days** on average. **Learning & Certification** is the quickest (**4.2 days**) and **WFH Equipment** the slowest (**4.7 days**).
insights: Decision times are consistent across categories, between **4.2** and **4.7** days.

questions.q: How many claims were submitted too late?
questions.briefing: **764** claims (4.8%) were submitted after the allowed window. **95.2%** of claims are submitted on time.
insights: Most late claims are in **Internet / Broadband** (**293** claims).
Submit claims within 30 days (15 days for travel and entertainment) of the expense.

questions.q: Are employees claiming within the allowed limits?
questions.briefing: Most claims stay within policy: only **2,230** of 15,845 claims (14.1%) asked for more than the limit. **WFH Equipment** has the most over-limit claims (**35.5%** of its claims).
insights: Limits apply per month, per claim, per year or once — depending on the category (see the policy table).
Amounts above the limit are not paid; only the limit amount is approved.

questions.q: Which departments claim the most?
questions.briefing: **Engineering** claims the most (**₹76.1 L**, 35% of the total) simply because it is the largest team. Hover to see all departments.
insights: Sales and Customer Success have extra categories like client entertainment and travel.

questions.q: What is the limit for each type of claim?
questions.briefing: There are **9 claim types**, each with its own limit, submission window and approver. Small monthly claims (internet, mobile, gym) are approved by your manager; big ones also need Finance.

rows: New joiners relocating within 3 months of joining

insights: Claims above the receipt threshold must have a receipt attached, or they will be rejected.

questions.q: Which documents do employees ask for the most (salary slip, Form 16, letters)?
questions.briefing: **2,168** documents were requested. **Relieving Letter** is asked for most (**356**), then **Experience Letter** and **Employment Verification Letter**.
insights: Letters for exiting employees (Relieving, Experience) are the most requested documents.

questions.q: Which documents are delivered within the promised time?
questions.briefing: **84%** of documents were delivered within the promised time. **Visa Support Letter** is the most reliable (**91.3%**) and **Form 16 (Tax Certificate)** the least (**71.0%**).
insights: Promised times range from **1 day** (payslip copy) to **7 days** (relieving letter).

questions.q: How many document requests come in each month?
questions.briefing: HR receives about **101** document requests a month. The busiest month was **July 2026** with **204** requests.
insights: Monthly requests grew from about **66** in early 2025 to about **138** in the latest six full months.

questions.q: How long does HR take to give a document, compared to the promised time?
questions.briefing: On average HR issues a document in **2.5 working days**. Compare the actual time with the promised time for each document below.
insights: Documents needing HR Business Partner approval take longer than portal downloads.

questions.q: How many document requests are still waiting, and for how long?
questions.briefing: **8** document requests are still open. The oldest has been waiting **3 working days**; the average wait is **1.5 days**.
insights: Only a handful of requests are open — almost everything is delivered quickly.

questions.q: Why do employees ask for documents (loan, visa, new job...)?
questions.briefing: The top reason for asking a document is **joining a new employer** (**35%** of requests), followed by **loan application** and **income tax filing**.
insights: Top 10 reasons shown. Employees leaving the company account for the largest share.

questions.q: How are documents sent (email, portal, hard copy)?
questions.briefing: **68%** of documents are sent as an email PDF and **28%** are downloaded from the portal. Only **95** needed a hard copy by courier.
insights: Digital delivery is instant and free — hard copies are only sent when specifically requested.

questions.q: Which HR team members handle the most document requests?
questions.briefing: **Sarah Saxena** handled the most document requests (**103**). Work is shared among **38** HR team members.
insights: Top 10 team members shown.

questions.q: How many HR policies do we have, and in which areas?
questions.briefing: HR has **20 approved policies** across **11** areas. **Benefits** has the most (**4**), covering health, life, provident fund and wellbeing. The AI helpdesk answers only from these approved policies.
insights: Every policy has an owner department, a version number and a yearly review date.

questions.q: Which policies are due for a review?
questions.briefing: **3** of 20 policies are overdue for their yearly review: **Holiday and Working Hours Policy, Code of Conduct and POSH Policy, Maternity, Paternity and Special Leave Policy**. The rest are up to date.

insights: Policies are reviewed every 12 months. Overdue ones should be re-approved so the AI helpdesk keeps giving current answers.

questions.briefing: The most-read question in the last 90 days is “**When do salary increments take effect?**” with **363 views**. The top 10 questions make up **44%** of all FAQ views.

questions.q: How many people work here, and how many have left?
questions.briefing: **1,442** people work at the company today. **819** have left since 2020. In the last 12 months **353** people left, an attrition rate of about **30%**.
insights: Joined in the last 12 months: **917** people.

questions.q: How has the company grown since 2020?
questions.briefing: The company has grown from **23** people in early 2020 to **1,442** today — **63×** larger. Growth was fastest in **Q3 '26**.
insights: Headcount counts everyone who had joined and not yet left at the end of each quarter.

questions.q: How many people are in each department?
questions.briefing: **Engineering** is the largest team with **489** people (**34%** of the company), followed by **Quality Assurance** and **AI / ML**.
insights: Tech teams together make up **72%** of all employees.

questions.q: How many men and women are in each department?
questions.briefing: **39%** of employees are women. **Information Security** has the highest share of women (**44.2%**) and **Finance & Admin** the lowest (**28.0%**).
insights: 13 employees identify as other.

questions.q: How many are freshers, mid-level or senior?
questions.briefing: **44%** of the team are freshers or interns and **9%** are senior or lead, so the company has a young workforce.
insights: Experience level is the level at which a person was hired.

questions.q: Where do people work (offices) and how (onsite, hybrid, remote)?
questions.briefing: **68%** of people work in a hybrid mode. **Hyderabad (HQ)** is the biggest office with **593** people.
insights: Work mode is the arrangement recorded in each employee's HR profile.

questions.q: How many new joiners have been confirmed after probation?
questions.briefing: **61%** of employees are confirmed. **457** are still on probation and **29** had their probation extended.
insights: Probation is 6 months for full-time employees; interns have no probation.

questions.q: How long have employees been with the company?
questions.briefing: The average employee has been here **1.3 years**. **53%** joined in the last year, while **53** people have more than 5 years of service.
insights: The company has hired heavily in the last two years, so many employees are still new.

questions.q: How are employees rated in their performance reviews?
questions.briefing: Of **653** employees with an appraisal, **45%** meet expectations (rating 3) and **34%** score 4 or 5. Only **6.7%** are rated 1.
insights: Interns and employees who joined recently have no rating yet, so they are not counted.

questions.q: Which tax option do employees choose (old or new)?
questions.briefing: **70%** of employees have chosen the **new tax regime** and **30%** stay on the old regime, which allows deductions such as 80C and HRA.
insights: Employees choose their regime in the HR portal at the start of each financial year; the new regime is the default.

questions.q: How many job openings are open, and how many have been filled?
questions.briefing: There have been **1,029** job openings since 2020. **60** are open right now and **925** were fully filled. Overall **93%** of the positions we opened have been filled.
insights: **41** openings were cancelled before being filled.
Open positions are mostly in **Engineering** and **AI / ML**.

questions.q: How many people apply, get interviewed, get offers and finally join?
questions.briefing: Of **53,183** applications, **41%** were shortlisted, **5.9%** received an offer and **2,238** people (**4.2%**) finally joined. That is about **1 hire for every 24 applications**.
insights: **82%** of offers were accepted and **87%** of those who accepted actually joined.

questions.q: How many job applications do we get each month?
questions.briefing: Applications have grown from **1,942** in 2020 to **13,045** in 2025. The busiest month ever was **July 2026** with **2,422** applications.

questions.q: Where do our best candidates come from (portal, referral, agency...)?
questions.briefing: **Employee Referral** is both our biggest source (**641** hires) and our best-quality one — **8.14%** of its applicants get hired.
insights: Hire rate = hires ÷ applicants. Job boards convert only about **2.8%**, far below referrals and campus drives.

questions.q: How much does it cost to hire one person from each source?
questions.briefing: Hiring through **Career Portal** is the cheapest (**₹1.5K per hire**). **Recruitment Agency** is the most expensive at **₹2.3 L** per hire. Total estimated sourcing cost is **₹5.20 Cr**.
insights: Cost = subscription or drive fees per hire, agency fee (8.33% of CTC) or referral bonus based on the hire's level.

questions.q: Which jobs take the longest to fill?
questions.briefing: A role takes **62 days** to fill on average. **Cloud Engineer** is the hardest to fill (**71 days**) and **ML Engineer** the quickest (**48 days**).
insights: Top 12 slowest roles shown. Senior and specialist roles take longer than entry-level ones.

questions.q: How many job openings took longer than planned?
questions.briefing: **506** of 988 job openings (51%) took longer than the planned closing date. **49%** were filled on time.
insights: Each opening has a target close date set when it is approved; delays usually come from hard-to-find skills.

questions.q: Why are candidates rejected, and at which step?
questions.briefing: **65%** of rejections happen at resume screening. The top reason is "**Profile not matching JD**" (**41%**), followed by "**Insufficient relevant experience**".
insights: Read left to right: where in the process candidates were rejected, and why.
Candidates who withdrew or declined offers are not counted here.

questions.q: Which departments hire the most people?
questions.briefing: **Engineering** has hired the most people (**841**, 38% of all hires), followed by **Quality Assurance** and **Data & Analytics**.
insights: Counts everyone hired through the recruitment process since 2020.

questions.q: How much salary do candidates ask for compared to what they earn now?
questions.briefing: Candidates expect a **36.5%** salary jump on average, and the ask is similar at every experience level. In rupees it differs a lot: a 12+ year candidate expects **₹67.2 L** a year versus **₹11.0 L** for a 0–1 year candidate.
insights: Based on candidates who are currently employed (current pay above zero).
L = Lakh per year.

questions.q: How many candidates pass each interview round?
questions.briefing: **72.9%** of candidates pass the HR screening, but only **54.0%** clear Technical Round 1. The strictest round is **Technical Round 1** with a **54.0%** pass rate.
insights: Based on **39,540** completed interviews with a result.

questions.q: How long does it take to share interview feedback?
questions.briefing: Candidates wait **3.8 days** on average between steps, and **38%** of interviews happen later than planned. Feedback is shared **0.7 days** after the interview.
insights: Wait = days since the previous step (shortlisting or the earlier round).

questions.q: Which employees take the most interviews?
questions.briefing: **Arjun Ghosh** has taken the most interviews (**4,012**). The top 10 interviewers together handled **40%** of all panel slots.
insights: Counts every time someone sat on an interview panel.

questions.q: How many job offers were accepted, declined, or not joined?
questions.briefing: Out of **3,159** offers, **71%** ended with the person joining. **16%** of candidates declined and **177** accepted but never turned up.
insights: Acceptance rate: **82%** of offers were accepted.

questions.q: How big is the salary hike we offer, and is it within budget?
questions.briefing: Offers come with an average salary hike of **37.2%** (typical: **35.1%**). **100%** of offers stay within the approved budget.
insights: Hike is measured against the candidate's current pay; freshers with no current pay are excluded.

questions.q: How many days do candidates take to decide, and to actually join?
questions.briefing: Candidates take **4.0 days** to answer an offer and **46.7 days** from offer to joining. **Lead** hires take the longest to join (**64.7 days**) because of notice periods.
insights: Interns and freshers join fastest; experienced hires must serve notice periods first.
